personal_viewing_method: Rendered each original prerequisite SVG with Inkscape, then personally viewed both PNGs using tools.view_image in this review.

figures.notes: I see a top shared-rules box, a token selecting expert 1 and 3 via two arrows, four expert boxes, and the unused expert 2 and 4 still marked as requiring weight storage. The orange box separates all weights, work for this token, and dispatch cost. The bottom sentence says another token may select a different pair and the diagram does not assign subject expertise. All labels are readable and no arrow or text is clipped. This made the R.4 storage/computation distinction concrete.

I see the same input x split into a gray W path and blue A then B path. W stays fixed but still calculates Wx; A reduces dimensions, B restores output dimensions, and alpha/r scales the correction. Both paths meet at a plus sign and the displayed output is Wx + (alpha/r)BAx. The bottom states that only A and B update. All labels and arrows are readable. This clarified that a LoRA file cannot replace the original base.
